target_customer: Young professionals and students renting furnished rooms or homes for 1 to 12 months, and hosts listing them
problem: Finding medium term furnished housing and compatible housemates is hard; Kopa combined listings, roommate matching, booking and payment.
business_model: marketplace take rate on bookings and rent payments
product_category: medium term rental and roommate marketplace

founders.name: Zach Waterfield
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; listed as a former founder.

exit.reason: The company site says the platform is shutting down, will become inactive immediately, and records will be deleted. No date or cause is given.

competitors.name: Roomi
competitors.what: Roommate matching app with listing photos and dating app style profiles
competitors.funding_then: about 17M dollars per a Crunchbase News roundup

competitors.name: Common
competitors.what: Co-living operator that acquired the roommate subleasing startup Skylight

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard marketplace with listings, verification, booking and payments built initially as a final year engineering project.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided supply and demand could build liquidity, but roommate and rental listings were widely available elsewhere.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competing roommate and furnished rental players kept raising and expanding; Kopa's site later announced shutdown without an acquisition.

market_need_then: The founders reported struggling to find housing as students from 2012 to 2016, and the 2017 to 2019 press covered a boom in shared housing startups.

identity.voice_and_tone: Community and exploration language: 'exploration and community make people whole'.

rebrands.why: Not stated; the site only says it launched as PadPiper in October 2016 in San Francisco and was renamed later.

brand_strength.rationale: A short, clean name and a mission statement about community, but no press on the brand and other companies named Kopa exist.

outcome_analysis: Kopa began as PadPiper in 2016, joined YC Winter 2019 and received a 150K YC investment. A co-founder stepped back in August 2020 and the site later announced an immediate shutdown with no stated cause. The failure factor is an inference from no found later round, and the 2020 pandemic's effect on medium term rentals is plausible but not sourced.
notes: The seed round rests on CB Insights and Seedtable; Seedtable reports three rounds without details, so funding may be incomplete. CB Insights lists a different founder name (Christine Olory) that could not be verified and was not used. Company site names three unnamed co-founders; only Waterfield is named on the YC page. The co-founder's Contra post (August 2020 step back) was seen only in a search summary because the fetch was rate limited. Roomi funding figure comes from a roundup seen in search results, not opened.
